About the conference

Connecting data, foresight and decision-making

Africa is experiencing profound and accelerating change — demographic growth, technological transformation, climate pressures, shifting geopolitics and evolving development pathways are reshaping the continent's future in complex, interconnected ways.

Convened by the African Futures and Innovation (AFI) programme at the Institute for Security Studies (ISS), the conference brings together policymakers, researchers, development practitioners, private-sector leaders and civil-society actors to explore how foresight can support better decisions for Africa's future.

Now in its third year, the conference connects research, foresight and policy engagement — with the practical application of long-term thinking at its centre.

At a glance
  • Dates 13–14 October 2026
  • Day 1 CSIR ICC, Pretoria + livestream
  • Day 2 Fully online, continent-wide
The theme

From Data to Decisions

Africa's future will be shaped by the choices made today. The 2026 theme carries that arc — from the evidence, through the alternatives, to the action.

1

Understanding Trends

Data, modelling and analysis reveal where Africa's development trajectory is currently heading.

2

Exploring Alternatives

Foresight opens up the futures that could emerge from different policy and strategic choices.

3

Shaping Futures

Turning insight into the decisions that build more inclusive, sustainable and resilient futures.

Conference format

A connected two-day experience

Strategic dialogue, practical learning and continent-wide participation — designed as one connected experience across two days.

Day 1 · 13 October

High-Level Dialogue & Strategic Engagement

Hybrid — CSIR ICC, Pretoria + livestream

Keynote addresses, strategic dialogues and panel discussions bringing together policymakers, thought leaders, researchers, development partners, private-sector representatives and practitioners around emerging trends and the strategic choices shaping Africa's future.

Opening Keynote

Africa’s Future

Dr Vera Songwe (TBC)

09:45–11:15

Session 1 · Understanding Trends

“Africa’s Current Path: Where are today’s trends taking us?”

An evidence-based presentation followed by a discussion of Africa’s current trajectory. Drawing on data, forecasting, modelling and scenario analysis, the session examines key trends shaping the continent — economic growth, employment, human development, demographics, governance and broader structural change.

Moderator: Ottilia Anna Maunganidze, ISS · Presentation: Dr Jakkie Cilliers, Head of African Futures & Innovation, ISS · Panel: Peter Engbo Rasmussen (African Development Bank), Amit Jain (NTU–SBF Centre for African Studies), Koffi Kouakou (University of Johannesburg)

11:15–11:45

Networking Break

11:45–13:00

Session 2 · Exploring Alternatives

“Alternative Futures: What could change Africa’s trajectory?”

A forward-looking discussion exploring how Africa’s future could unfold differently under changing policy, leadership, innovation, investment, institutional and global conditions. Experts will challenge assumptions, explore alternative pathways and identify the decisions and disruptions that could fundamentally alter future outcomes.

Moderator: Bronwyn Williams, Partner & Futurist, Flux Trends · Panel: Dr Trish Lavery (Centre for Future Generations), Dr Kagiso “TK” Pooe (African School of Governance), Professor Adrian Saville (Gordon Institute of Business Science, University of Pretoria)

13:00–14:00

Lunch & Networking

14:00–16:00

Session 3 · Shaping Futures

“Shaping Africa’s Future: From Preferred Futures to Strategic Choices”

An intergenerational and interactive conversation about the futures Africans want and the choices required to move towards them, bringing together established leaders and emerging voices — including the Top 5 Young Changemakers 2026 — to explore what more inclusive, prosperous, sustainable and resilient African futures could look like.

Moderator: Dr Njeri Mwagiru, SAIIA · Panel: Amb. Salah Hammad (AU, TBC), Jacques Morisset (World Bank), Elijah Koome (Top 5 Young Changemaker 2026), Ndum Charlotte Ayeah (Top 5 Young Changemaker 2026)

16:00–17:30

Networking Reception & Book Launch

Live music by Justin Zulu. Launch of “Africa’s Road to Prosperity – 10 Things to Know”: Dr Jakkie Cilliers in conversation with Dr Ayanda Ntsaluba, Executive Director, Discovery Limited & Member of the ISS Board of Trustees.

Confirmed speakers

Additional speakers and session contributors will be announced as the programme is finalised.

Jacques Morisset
Lead Economist for South Africa, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho & Namibia · World Bank

Holds a PhD in economics from the University of Geneva and has held various positions at the World Bank Group, advising governments on growth, financial markets, investment promotion, fiscal and tax policies, and labor markets. Published in the World Bank Economic Review, Journal of Development Economics and World Development; former Board member of the World Bank Economic Review.

Amit Jain
Frontier Markets Specialist · former Director, NTU-SBF Centre for African Studies · LinkedIn ↗

A leading authority on African issues in Southeast Asia with a 25+ year career mobilising private-sector investment across frontier markets. Author of Back to Growth: Priority Agenda for the Economic Revival of Nigeria and recipient of the 2005 UK Panos-GKP Award. Non-resident fellow at the Africa Policy Research Institute and 2026 global visiting fellow at the John Curtin Institute of Public Policy, Curtin University.

Jakkie Cilliers
Founder & Head, African Futures & Innovation Programme · Chair, ISS Board of Trustees

Founder and former Executive Director of the ISS; extraordinary professor at the University of Pretoria. Author of Fate of the Nation and the Africa Tomorrow book series, including Africa’s Road to Prosperity: 10 Things to Know, launched at AFC 2026.

Day 2 · 14 October

Practice, Participation & Learning

Fully online — open continent-wide

Workshops, futures lab sessions, practical demonstrations, case studies and lightning talks designed to strengthen foresight skills, share practical tools and encourage peer learning across the continent.

Confirmed speakers & facilitators

Room assignments and remaining TBC chairs will be confirmed closer to the event.

Andrés Felipe Olarte Peña
PhD Candidate, Technische Universität Berlin

Andrés Felipe Olarte is a PhD candidate at Technische Universität Berlin working on climate policy, sustainability and computational social science. His research explores how evidence, modelling and emerging technologies can support policy decisions under uncertainty. He has professional experience in carbon pricing, emissions trading and international climate cooperation. His interests include anticipatory governance, green industrialisation, climate finance, just transitions and scenario-based approaches to long-term planning.

Anum Khan
Associate Fellow, National Maritime Foundation

Anum Khan is an Associate Fellow at the National Maritime Foundation (NMF), where she is part of the Indian and Regional Maritime Security Cluster. Her research focuses on the Djibouti Code of Conduct and its Jeddah Amendments (DCoC-JA), the Indian Ocean Commission (IOC) Member States, and the maritime geostrategies of Eastern African coastal and island States. She holds an M.A. in Politics (International and Area Studies) from Jamia Millia Islamia and an M.Phil. in African Studies from the University of Delhi, where she is currently pursuing a PhD on conflict dynamics in the Liptako–Gourma region.

Dominique Dryding
Capacity Building Manager, Afrobarometer

Dominique Dryding is the Afrobarometer Capacity Building Manager, where she leads initiatives that strengthen the use of citizen-generated evidence among policymakers, civil society organisations, journalists, researchers, universities and Afrobarometer network partners. She designs and facilitates capacity-building programmes across numerous African countries and leads the development of Afrobarometer’s digital learning resources. Her work explores how public opinion data can strengthen democratic governance, deepen civic engagement, and contribute to informed conversations about Africa’s future.

Eli Ocen
UN Youth Delegate for Uganda; AI & Digital Governance Researcher

Eli Haggai Ocen is the United Nations Youth Delegate for the Republic of Uganda, a technology and digital governance practitioner and a researcher specialising in AI for information integrity, diplomacy and peacebuilding. He previously served with the UN Department of Peace Operations’ Information Integrity Unit, addressing mis-, dis- and malinformation and hate speech in peacekeeping contexts. His work focuses on applying open-source data, digital analytics and strategic foresight to strengthen governance, peacebuilding and youth participation in Africa.

Gawah Tafon Emmanuel Babila
FinTech Architect & Founder, Cameroon FinTech Lab

Gawah Emmanuel is a FinTech Architect, Researcher, Policy Analyst, and the Founder of the Cameroon FinTech Lab (CFL). A Chevening Scholar with an MSc in Financial Technology from Manchester Metropolitan University, he works at the convergence of digital finance, market infrastructure, data-driven policymaking and strategic foresight. Through the Lab, he leads strategic policy dialogue, regulatory advocacy and research on open finance, interoperability and financial inclusion, and convenes policymakers, regulators and innovators through the FinTech Chat.

Gerald Macheka
Senior Economist & Chief Editor, Equity Axis

Gerald Hatirutyi Macheka is an economist, researcher and research communicator, and an MSc Economics candidate at the University of Zimbabwe. He serves as Senior Economist and Chief Editor at Equity Axis, a Zimbabwean financial research and advisory firm, where he leads economic research, data analysis and communication for policymakers, businesses and the public across Southern Africa. His research interests include international trade, industrial policy, economic development, climate finance and structural transformation.

Habmo Birwe
Research, Evaluation & Policy Consultant — Migration & Climate Mobility

Habmo Birwe is a Research, Evaluation and Policy Consultant specialising in migration, climate mobility and social inclusion across Africa. He has over five years of experience supporting international organisations including the World Bank, IOM, the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie and FEMNET on displacement, fragility and climate governance, with particular emphasis on the Sahel and Central Africa. He is a member of the Steering Group of the Climate Mobility Africa Research Network (CMARN).

Ismail Numan Telci
Professor of International Relations, Ibn Haldun University

Ismail Numan Telci is Professor of International Relations at Ibn Haldun University, Turkey, and Director of the Center for Gulf Studies and Global Policy. His research focuses on Middle East and Gulf geopolitics, Turkish foreign policy and regional security architecture. He has authored six books and numerous policy reports, and his commentary has featured in Anadolu Agency, TRT World, Al Jazeera, BBC and Deutsche Welle.

Jackline Musuya
Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning Lead, Hewatele Limited

Jackline Musuya is a Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning professional, researcher and emerging scholar with over ten years of experience supporting evidence generation, organisational learning and strategic decision-making across health, cooperative development, WASH and market systems programmes in East Africa. She is a Women in Leadership and Development (WILD) Network Fellow and an Online Monitoring and Learning Academy (OMLA) Fellow.

Jaynisha Patel
Senior Analyst, Tony Blair Institute for Global Change

Jaynisha Patel is a Senior Analyst and in-house Africa expert at the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, specialising in African geopolitics and geoeconomics. She advises senior political leaders across Africa, the Gulf and Europe on geostrategy and foreign policy, and briefs TBI’s executive leadership on geopolitical and political-economy developments. Her analysis has featured on the BBC World Service, Voice of America, Foreign Policy and Project Syndicate.

Jerome Arab
PhD Researcher, War Studies, King’s College London

Jerome Arab is a PhD Researcher in the War Studies Department at King’s College London, based at the Leverhulme Centre for Research on Slavery in War. His doctoral research investigates how Congolese women in Solwezi, Zambia, use narrative practices to anticipate and navigate risks of conflict-related sexual slavery. He is the creator of The Copper Bullet Thesis and Founder of Underrated Individuals Ltd, bringing over two decades of experience in filmmaking, theatre and community development across Africa and the UK.

Jonathan Powell
Associate Professor of Political Science, Campbellsville University

Jonathan Powell is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Campbellsville University and a Research Fellow at the University of Kentucky’s Patterson School of Diplomacy. He is co-creator of the Global Instances of Coups dataset and current director of Mutiny Monitor, a collaborative effort to forecast military coups and their consequences. He has presented research at the Atlantic Council, the U.S. State Department, the National Intelligence Council and the Institute for Security Studies.

Londiwe Buthelezi
Assistant Lecturer, University of Pretoria

Londiwe Buthelezi is a junior researcher and policy professional focused on digital democracy, democratic institutions and modelling pathways to alternate futures. Her master’s dissertation used backcasting to explore the feasibility of electronic voting in South Africa’s 2034 elections. She is currently an Assistant Lecturer for Political Science and International Relations at the University of Pretoria and a Research Fellow for the Africa Political Outlook (APO).

Maclaren Murimba
Executive Director, Global Deaf Network (Zimbabwe)

Maclaren Murimba is a youth leader and the Executive Director of Global Deaf Network (GDN) in Zimbabwe. He is passionate about disability inclusion, youth empowerment and community development, with a strong commitment to ensuring Deaf youth and other marginalised groups have equal opportunities to participate in leadership and decision-making, through inclusive programmes spanning climate action, entrepreneurship, health and governance.

Margherita Fadda
Policy Analyst, OECD Sahel and West Africa Club

Margherita Fadda is a policy analyst at the OECD, in the Sahel and West Africa Club Secretariat. She analyses urban dynamics on the African continent and contributes to the Africa’s Urbanisation Dynamics report series and the Africapolis programme.

Mayada Mohammed
Urban Planning Researcher

Mayada Mohammed is an urban planning researcher focused on evidence-based planning, neighbourhood livability and adaptive governance across rapidly changing African cities. Her doctoral research in post-conflict Sudan explores how daily resident adaptations in planned neighbourhoods can generate spatial intelligence to guide regulatory reforms. Bringing together GIS-based spatial analytics, mixed-methods fieldwork and policy evaluation, her work bridges urban theory and practical foresight.

Nancy Kgengwenyane
Environmental & Natural Resources Lawyer

Nancy Kgengwenyane is an environmental and natural resources lawyer working in international environmental law, climate justice, critical minerals governance and the legal architecture underpinning African sovereignty in trade, resource and data governance. As Senior Associate at Innolead Consulting Africa’s Sustainability & Governance Unit, she advises governments, private-sector actors and civil society organisations on ESG and sustainable development frameworks.

Nixon Nembaware
Governance, Gender & Resilience Specialist

Nixon Nembaware is a governance, gender and resilience specialist with over 15 years of experience supporting governments, UN agencies and international development organisations across Southern Africa. He developed the Gender Norm Score I & II (GNS-I & II), an evidence-based framework measuring social norm change, adopted by a UNDP programme in Zimbabwe and other development agencies. His current research explores how social norm data can support anticipatory governance and strategic foresight.

Nsah Mala
Foresight Practitioner, Universities of Lille & Cologne

Dr Nsah Mala (Kenneth Nsah) is a multiple award-winning Cameroonian researcher and foresight practitioner working at the intersection of sustainability science, participatory foresight, governance and long-term policy design across Africa. He is affiliated with the Universities of Lille and Cologne, UNESCO-MOST BRIDGES Coalition and the Nkafu Policy Institute, and was recognised at the 2025 Dubai Foresight Awards for participatory scenario-building work across the Congo Basin.

Per Ostberg
Strategic Foresight Consultant
“Foresight in practice – Challenges to move from Insights to Actions”
Speaking in: Plenary: What Data Alone Cannot Solve — Signals in Seven II

Over the past 30+ years, Per Ostberg has worked across Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East as a strategic foresight consultant, project director for multinationals, and entrepreneur, living and working in over 90 countries. As a foresight consultant, he helps leaders and executive teams think differently about the future by applying foresight thinking tools to signals, trends and events to identify opportunities and risks that might otherwise remain hidden. He also coaches teams and leaders on building effective multicultural organisations.

Pierre-Christophe Gam
Founder, TOGUNA WORLD

Pierre-Christophe Gam is a transdisciplinary artist, researcher and foresight practitioner working at the intersection of African cosmology, speculative design and anticipatory governance. Trained in architecture at ENSAD Paris and Central Saint Martins, he is the founder of TOGUNA WORLD, an international art and research platform behind The Global Mapping of Dreams, a participatory foresight project active across 13 African nations and the diaspora. His work has been exhibited at Ars Electronica, the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao and the Vitra Design Museum.

Salah Ben Hammou
Postdoctoral Research Associate, Rice University’s Baker Institute

Dr Salah Ben Hammou is a Postdoctoral Research Associate at Rice University’s Baker Institute for Public Policy and a Nonresident Fellow at the Centre for African Conflict and Development. His research focuses on political instability, civil-military relations and governance in Africa and the Middle East, with particular emphasis on military coups, post-coup politics and civilian agency. His work has informed policy discussions through Foreign Policy, the Washington Post and The Conversation.

Sara Tadesse Gebremariam
Independent Policy Researcher, Horn & East Africa

Sara Tadesse Gebremariam is an independent policy researcher and consultant specialising in conflict analysis, peacebuilding and transitional justice across the Horn of Africa and East Africa, with particular depth in Ethiopia, Sudan and South Sudan. She holds an MSc in Global Leadership and Peacebuilding from King’s College London and a BA from SOAS, and is currently developing a research initiative on integrating CRSV accountability into DDR processes in post-conflict Ethiopia.

Sethu Nguna
Training & Instructional Design Manager, AidData Research Lab

Sethu Nguna is Training and Instructional Design Manager at AidData Research Lab, an instructional and learning systems specialist with over a decade of experience designing immersive, data-informed learning environments that help practitioners and decision-makers test assumptions and adapt to complexity. She developed Plenum, an interactive simulation platform with the William & Mary Statecraft Simulation Group, and has delivered learning initiatives across Pakistan, the Philippines and the Mandela Washington Fellowship.

Steven Lichty
Director, Frontline Futures

Dr Steven Lichty is the director of Frontline Futures, a boutique firm focused on transformative foresight in Nairobi, Kenya. He has 25 years’ experience across Africa, Asia, Europe and Latin America, including post-conflict, transitional and fragile environments, working with strategic foresight, futures thinking, organisational development and systems mapping. Steven holds a PhD in African Studies and an MPhil in Futures Studies from Stellenbosch Business School, and currently researches vision statements of African states.

Tanja Hichert
Fellow, Centre for Sustainability Transitions, Stellenbosch University

Tanja Hichert is a futures/foresight and systems-thinking practitioner with over 20 years’ experience running Hichert & Associates. She is a Fellow at the Centre for Sustainability Transitions at Stellenbosch University, where she co-chairs the UNESCO Chair in Complex Systems and Transformative African Futures, and previously served as Strategic Foresight Advisor to UNDP HQ. She recently co-authored the UNESCO MOST policy paper Social Investment Across Africa’s Demographic Transitions.

Tatjana von Bormann
Co-Founder & Co-Director, Southern Africa Food Lab

Tatjana von Bormann co-founded and co-directs the Southern Africa Food Lab, Africa’s longest-running multi-stakeholder platform for food systems change, an initiative of Stellenbosch University. She holds an MPhil in Future Studies (Cum Laude) from Stellenbosch Business School and has applied Three Horizons and related foresight tools across food systems and non-profit settings, drawing on 25 years of experience including a multi-year corporate partnership at WWF South Africa.

Tsakane Matsilele
Researcher, National Strategic Hub

Tsakane Matsilele is a researcher with the National Strategic Hub, with a background in policy and research. Her current work focuses on analysing spatial transformation in South Africa and developing practical, data-driven guides that help municipal planners strengthen evidence-based planning. She is particularly passionate about the intersection of digital transformation and social justice, examining how emerging technologies and data systems can either reinforce or reduce vulnerability for marginalised communities.

Victoria Olaonipekun
Project & Programme Associate, TechCabal

Victoria Olaonipekun is a PMP-certified project and programme associate working at the intersection of technology, education and entrepreneurship in Africa. At TechCabal, she supports the design and delivery of ecosystem programmes including Moonshot by TechCabal and TC Battlefield, convening founders, investors, policymakers and emerging talent. She has also coordinated inclusive women-in-STEM programmes with WeTech and supported the Mastercard Foundation EdTech Conference.

Thematic tracks

Five lenses on Africa's future

Across all tracks, the conference promotes diverse voices and intergenerational dialogue on shaping the continent's future.

Africa's current path & development potential

An evidence-based look at where current trends are likely to lead — economic growth, employment, human development, governance, demographics and food systems.

Alternative futures

How Africa's future could unfold differently — the role of policy, leadership, innovation, investment and institutions in shaping alternative pathways.

Preferred futures for Africa

What inclusive, sustainable and desirable futures could look like, connecting closely with Agenda 2063 and continental development aspirations.

Building futures capacity

Hands-on futures lab sessions and workshops covering futures literacy, scenario development, horizon scanning and participatory foresight.

Foresight for decision-making & impact

Real-world examples of foresight informing policy — integrating foresight into national planning and institutionalising it within government.

Young Changemakers 2026

The Choices That Will Shape Africa's Future

Building on previous editions, the conference once again elevates the voices and ideas of emerging African leaders. Selected Young Changemakers are featured during the conference, engaging directly with policymakers, researchers and fellow participants — strengthening intergenerational dialogue and African agency in shaping the future.
